content.text: {"relation":"REFINED","consensus_summary":"All four blind responses converge on a settled core: swine symbolize uncleanness and spiritual/moral impurity rooted in the Levitical food laws (Lev 11:7; Deut 14:8), applied in the NT to the profane person who tramples holy things (Matt 7:6) and the apostate returning to filth (2 Pet 2:22). Common alternatives include Gentiles/pagans, apostates, gluttony/sensuality, demonic association (Gadarene swine), and the destructive boar of Ps 80:13; one response notes a hypocrisy reading from the parted-hoof-without-cud-chewing detail.","book_summary":"The book keeps the unclean-beast core but sharpens it in two ways: (1) the pig is the beast wearing the outward sign (parted hoof) without the inward work (no cud-chewing), i.e., false outward conformity; and (2) it identifies the swine specifically as the nation outside the covenant — Gentiles — who trample what is holy, linking Matt 7:6's trampled pearls to Rev 11:2's Gentiles treading the holy city, and folding the washed sow of 2 Pet 2:22 into the same covenantal picture.","consensus_core_identification":"Uncleanness/spiritual impurity generally — the profane, unregenerate, or apostate person who scorns holy things.","book_core_identification":"The unclean beast marked by outward sign without inward reality, identified specifically as the Gentile nation outside the covenant that tramples what is holy.","core_relation":"BOOK_NARROWS","extension_relation":"PARTIAL_RECLASSIFICATION","boundary_disagreement":"The consensus treats swine broadly as any profane/unclean person (with Gentiles listed only as a common or minority alternative). The book elevates that alternative to the central identification and narrows the referent to the covenant-outsider nation. It reclassifies Matt 7:6's swine from 'unreceptive/profane people generally' to Gentiles specifically (via the trampling parallel with Rev 11:2), and reads 2 Pet 2:22's washed sow within the same national/covenantal frame rather than as the individual apostate. The hypocrisy detail (hoof without cud) is present in consensus only as a minority note but is made structural in the book.","material_contradiction":"","rationale":"The book preserves the consensus's general category — the swine as the unclean, profane trampler of holy things — so there is no replaced referent. But it materially changes precision and extension: what the consensus treats as a broad moral symbol with Gentile identification as one option among several becomes, in the book, a specific covenantal identification (the nation outside the covenant), supported by a novel Matt 7:6–Rev 11:2 trampling link. This is real boundary disagreement (which people/cases the symbol picks out) without contradiction of the core, matching REFINED with BOOK_NARROWS at the core and partial reclassification of the Matt 7:6 and 2 Pet 2:22 cases.","citation_support":"PARTIAL","strongest_objection":"Against REFINED, one could argue MATCH: the Gentile/pagan identification appears explicitly as a listed alternative in Responses A, C, and D, and the hypocrisy reading appears in Response B, so every element of the book's entry is already within the consensus map. The rebuttal is that the book does not merely include these as options — it makes the covenant-outsider nation the central identification and reclassifies the standard referents of Matt 7:6 and 2 Pet 2:22 accordingly, and the Rev 11:2 linkage (a verse with no swine) is a lexical inference the consensus does not make.","confidence":"medium"}
